title: The Best Postpartum Underwear, Ranked (2026)
summary: Discover the best postpartum underwear for every recovery stage, from soft post-surgery options to Honeylove’s targeted, stay-put everyday support.
body_markdown:
The SuperPower Brief uses targeted compression to shape the midsection, making it comfortable to wear all day. Honeylove offers five levels of support, and the SuperPower Brief is a level four: Strong Support garment.


The dominant feedback is praise for the product's hold-without-squeeze feel. Rather than compressing everywhere, Honeylove uses targeted panels that work strategically to give a sculpted silhouette. Multiple reviewers describe an hourglass shape without constriction. The distinction from all-over compression shapewear comes up again and again.


Stay-put construction is the second theme that matters for postpartum reviewers. In real-world wear testing, the shapewear did not roll down, which customers cite as a significant advantage.


The flexible boning is what keeps the brief from rolling down or bunching — a problem that plagues almost every other brand of shapewear. One reviewer and mom of three noted that the targeted compression was especially effective for the lower tummy, offering moderate hold right where it counts.


Best for:


Women who've finished early recovery and want a brief that provides real targeted compression and all-day support without shifting or squeezing. This is where recovery-specific underwear gives way to something you'll actually want to wear every day.


## #2 Bodily All-In Panty: Best overall recovery underwear


When you're ready to stop pulling on hospital mesh and start wearing something that actually feels like underwear again, the Bodily All-In Panty is the first real upgrade. It's the pair you reach for when you want something washable, genuinely soft, and built for a body that's still actively recovering.


Based on testing from 11 postpartum moms, survey feedback from over 300 community members, and advice from two OB-GYNs, The Bump chose the Bodily All-In Panty as the overall best postpartum underwear. It's their Best of The Bump award-winner for overall best postpartum underwear for the third year running.


**Here are the features and pricing:**


-


$15.85 single; S–L


-


Ultra-soft micromodal that feels gentle against healing skin, with a high-rise fit that avoids incision areas and provides light, supportive compression where it matters most


-


A wide gusset that offers enough coverage to comfortably hold a maxi pad , with a slightly cheeky rear


-


Ultra-stretchy details throughout, from the material itself to the leg openings, that accommodate postpartum swelling and size fluctuations


The dominant review pattern is softness against healing skin. When testing, the All-In Panty stood out among the rest because of how incredibly soft and stretchy it was.The wider leg openings made it possible to pull the pair over a postpartum belly with complete ease, without sagging or feeling loose.


Incision clearance is the second signal. The wide band elastic waist sits high enough to stay put on a pregnancy bump or healing core while covering a C-section incision without rubbing. Both C-section and vaginal delivery reviewers confirm this consistently.


Multiple buyers describe ordering in bulk after their first pair, turning it into a recovery staple rather than a one-off purchase.


One honest limitation surfaces in reviews: the underwear can ride up slightly on some body types, particularly those with longer inseams or curvier builds.


Best for:


Women who want washable, everyday-style postpartum underwear from day one of recovery through the early postpartum weeks.


## #3 Nyssa FourthWear Postpartum Recovery Underwear: Best for C-section and vaginal recovery


The Nyssa FourthWear earns its spot for a functional reason no other pick in this list can match: at its core is a patented dual-layer, 360° pocket system, engineered to hold ice or heat therapy securely against the body in three key zones. It was developed in collaboration with an Innovation Advisory Board of OB-GYNs, doulas, midwives, and pelvic floor therapists.


This is the acute-recovery specialist. It's built for weeks one and two, when ice and heat therapy are doing the most healing work — not the pair you graduate to.


**Here are the features and pricing:**


-


$39; XXS–4X


-


85% Recycled Polyester, 15% Spandex; seamless, adaptive compression


-


The pocket holds a pad on the inside of the underwear, so you can manage postpartum bleeding and apply cold or heat therapy at the same time, hands-free Designed specifically to provide comfort for both C-section and vaginal birth recoveries


-


High waist that folds down for flexibility as your body changes


-


FSA/HSA-eligible


Reviewers consistently describe the pocket system as a real upgrade over the improvised ice-pack-in-underwear approach. One buyer appreciated the pocket for the heating pack, noting it was "so helpful because I was also managing a baby without having to worry about the heating pack staying in place."


The 360-degree pocket holds ice or heat therapy at the incision site, around the back, or between the legs after a vaginal birth.


Both C-section and vaginal delivery users confirm the design works for either recovery path. One C-section reviewer called these "the only postpartum underwear that TRULY are for C-sections," noting that other "high-rise" options roll down and put pressure where it shouldn't be.


A small number of reviews flag a product longevity note: one buyer found the ice packs had lost their cooling capability by a second use two years later. If you're planning ahead for a second pregnancy, you may need replacement packs.


Best for:


Women in active early recovery, especially during the first one to two weeks when ice and heat therapy are most beneficial.


## #4 Kindred Bravely High-Waisted Postpartum Recovery Panties: Best budget multi-pack


If you're stocking a hospital bag or building a postpartum underwear rotation before your due date, Kindred Bravely is the pick for buying in volume without regret. The value here isn't disposability. It's reusability at scale — a five-pack of washable, stretchy briefs that you can rotate through daily without running the washing machine at 2 a.m.


**Here are the features and pricing:**


-


~$36 for a 5-pack; XS–1X


-


Premium viscose blend that's lightweight and ultra-stretchy


-


Wide lace waistband; high-rise cut sits above a C-section incision


-


Full-coverage cut with plenty of room for postpartum pads


The Bump names Kindred Bravely as its pick for best budget-friendly reusable postpartum underwear. Reviewers describe the fabric as conforming through postpartum body fluctuations without pinching or riding up.


The stretch accommodates the rapid size changes that happen in the first weeks. That's exactly what you want from a multi-pack you're buying before delivery.


The C-section clearance pattern is present here too. Multiple reviewers confirm the high waist sits above the incision without aggravating healing skin. The wide lace waistband gets praise from most buyers for its combination of stretch and softness.


One honest limitation: the lace waistband, while comfortable for most, is flagged by a minority of C-section reviewers as potentially irritating against very fresh surgical skin in the first few days post-op. For the earliest acute healing window, a seamless option like Nyssa or Bodily may be gentler. These are better suited to the days just after the most acute phase.


Best for:


Building a hospital bag and recovery stock without breaking the budget. Best bought in the 5-pack before delivery.


## #5 Belly Bandit C-Section Recovery Brief: Best dedicated C-section pick


This is the specialized tool for a specific window. While other picks on this list accommodate C-section recovery, the Belly Bandit brief is engineered around it. These briefs gently protect the incision area while silver-infused fibers help eliminate bacteria and odor.


That antimicrobial construction sets it apart from every other pick here. It's purpose-built for the approximately one-to-six-week surgical healing window.


**Here are the features and pricing:**


-


$34.95; S–XL; Black and Nude


-


Designed with Stayput technology to prevent rolling and uncomfortable pinching, sewn with soft fabrics blended with silver-infused yarns to help minimize odor and prevent bacteria


-


Light compression, high-waisted for full incision coverage


-


Moisture-wicking for all-day freshness


-


Eligible for reimbursement from FSA/HSA accounts and a number of U.S. health insurance companies


The dominant review pattern is incision protection confidence. One verified reviewer confirmed: "It protects my C-section incision and allows me to comfortably wear pants and leggings over them." A first-time C-section mom shared that she started wearing them two weeks post-surgery and regretted not starting sooner. She strongly recommended getting them on as quickly as possible for the support they provide when getting out of bed.


The honest negative to flag: this item is non-returnable and non-exchangeable. That means sizing errors are one-way mistakes. Belly Bandit recommends going one size up from your pre-pregnancy size. Measure carefully before you order.


Best for:


Women recovering from a C-section who want dedicated incision protection and antimicrobial fabric during the surgical healing window.


## #6 HATCH Collection Seamless Belly Brief: Best light-compression transition pick


There's a specific gap between acute recovery gear and everyday underwear that doesn't get enough attention. At six to twelve weeks postpartum, you're done with medical-grade recovery underwear. But you may not be ready for firm compression either.


The HATCH Seamless Belly Brief is the intentional bridge — the right pick for a different phase.


**Here are the features and pricing:**


-


$38; S–XL


-


Available in Black, Nude, Sand, Pink Lemonade


-


Soft, breathable modal blend with a seamless, finely ribbed texture that smooths and lightly sculpts without feeling restrictive


-


High-waisted silhouette with full coverage that stays in place with no riding up or bunching; seamless, ribbed construction designed for third trimester through postpartum recovery


-


OEKO-TEX certified fabric


The Bump awarded these a Best of The Bump award for best postpartum underwear with light compression. In real-world testing, a product tester reported that the "light compression felt supportive without being too tight, especially around my lower belly," and that it "genuinely helped hold pads in place better than regular underwear."


Stretchiness is a secondary positive. One tester noted the material is "so stretchy" that she could've sized down, and that this flexibility made it "super easy to put on" during the early postpartum period. The honest tradeoff is that the compression is genuinely light. Reviewers who want firmer support say this doesn't deliver enough. If you're looking for real midsection hold, this isn't your pick — it's a smoother, not a sculptor.


Best for:


Women six to twelve weeks postpartum who want gentle compression without the firmness of shapewear. A soft transition brief, not a permanent solution.


## When you're ready for Honeylove


There's a point, once your provider clears everyday activity, when recovery-specific underwear has done its job. The ice pockets are in the drawer. The disposables are in the trash.


Your body is still different than it was, and it deserves something built for this version of you.


The Honeylove SuperPower Brief is the shaping underwear a woman wears when she wants targeted hold and a smooth silhouette that actually stays put all day.


Engineered compression panel target the midsection without all-over constriction, so your changing body gets support where it needs it without that squeezed-everywhere feeling.


The flexible side boning keeps the garment from rolling down or bunching, even without a rubber grip at the waist. It stays put all day. And the fit holds across the size range, including postpartum sizes, with reviewers noting the brief fits true to size and provides supportive hold without being too tight.


Find your[perfect Honeylove size](https://www.honeylove.com/sizing) and make the switch from recovery to real, everyday support.

## Best postpartum underwear FAQs


Below are the questions we hear most from women navigating postpartum underwear decisions — from timing the switch away from disposables to figuring out how many pairs you actually need.


### When should I switch from disposable to reusable postpartum underwear?


Most women transition away from disposables within the first one to two weeks, once bleeding slows enough that you're using standard maxi pads rather than hospital-grade ones. A reusable pick like the Bodily All-In Panty or Kindred Bravely 5-pack can handle that level of protection while feeling significantly more comfortable against healing skin.


### What's the difference between postpartum underwear and regular shapewear?


Postpartum underwear prioritizes healing. It's built with higher rises to clear incisions, wider gussets for pads, and softer fabrics for sensitive skin.


Regular shapewear focuses on silhouette and compression for aesthetic purposes. A pick like the Honeylove SuperPower Brief bridges these worlds by offering targeted compression designed for all-day wear without the medical-recovery features (ice pockets, antimicrobial fibers) that early postpartum demands.


### How many pairs of postpartum underwear do I need?


Plan for five to seven pairs in rotation. Nyssa recommends purchasing at least three pairs so you always have a pair on hand while the others are in the laundry. If you're mixing recovery underwear (like Nyssa or Bodily) with a later-phase pick (like Honeylove), three of each gives you a full rotation without daily washes.
